summary: Mentra is building an AI-powered wearable assistant for deskless workers, starting with AR glasses for frontline manufacturing and logistics. The team has deep hardware + ML expertise (ex-Meta, Magic Leap, Apple), but the product is pre-revenue with an unproven go-to-market motion in a crowded AR/wearable landscape. Score: 51/100 — enough signal to track, not enough to commit.
rationale: Team (12/20): Strong technical pedigree in optics, computer vision, and embedded ML, but no prior commercial hardware ship experience and missing a seasoned GTM/sales leader. Defensibility (9/20): IP around low-latency on-device inference and ergonomic form factor is real but narrow; competitors (RealWear, Vuzix, TeamViewer, Microsoft) have deeper supply chains and channel relationships. Product (11/20): Prototype demonstrates compelling hands-free workflows (visual inspection, guided assembly), yet battery life (2.5 hrs) and thermal throttling remain unsolved for full-shift use. Market & Why-Now (10/20): Deskless workforce digitization is a $30B+ TAM tailwind, but budget cycles are long, IT security reviews are strict, and BYOD/phone-based solutions are 'good enough' for many use cases. Traction / Freshness (9/20): 3 paid pilots (2 in automotive, 1 in warehousing) with $0 ARR; pilot conversion timeline unclear. Freshness penalty: no new pilot signed in 4 months. Overall 51/100 reflects a credible wedge technology with execution risk concentrated in hardware reliability, channel access, and proof of repeatable sales motion.
changeMyMind: Signs 2+ pilots converting to paid deployments (>$50k ARR each) with 6-month renewal commitments
